title: Rescheduling an Appointment
setting: You need to move an appointment because something came up at work.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Hey, any chance I could push my appointment back a little?
dialogue.zh: 嗨，请问我能不能把预约稍微往后推一点？

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Sure. What time were you hoping for?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Would four-thirty work? Something came up at work.
dialogue.zh: 四点半可以吗？工作上临时出了点事。

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Let me check. Yeah, we can fit you in at four-thirty.
dialogue.zh: 我查一下。可以，我们能把你安排在四点半。

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Perfect. I appreciate it. Sorry for the last-minute change.
dialogue.zh: 太好了，非常感谢。不好意思这么临时改时间。

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: No worries. Just try to get here about ten minutes early.
dialogue.zh: 没关系。尽量提前十分钟左右到就行。

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Will do. Thanks for working with me.
dialogue.zh: 好的，会的。谢谢你愿意配合我调整。

expressions.note: A natural, polite way to ask for a favor or small accommodation.

expressions.zh: 临时有事 / 突然出了点状况。
expressions.note: Very common when you do not need to explain the details.
Common for appointments, doctors, salons, repairs, and schedules.

expressions.zh: 临时的；最后一刻才发生的。
expressions.note: Often used in phrases like a last-minute change or cancellation.

expressions.zh: 好的 / 没问题，我会的。
expressions.note: A concise, natural response after someone gives you a simple instruction.

exercise: You have a 3:00 PM dentist appointment, but something came up. Ask to move it to 4:00 PM in 2–3 natural English sentences. Try to use: Any chance I could…? / Something came up / Would four o’clock work?
